message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine appropriate crime(s) from list.

Facts: Li, an animal food inspection officer, forged false documents (the "China animal health supervision prohibited production, operation animal and product list") 27 copies, to help others obtain state financial subsidy for harmless disposal of 50 diseased pigs, amount 29,000 RMB.

So crime: forging official documents? The list includes "伪造、变造、买卖国家机关公文、证件、印章". That is forging, altering, buying/selling state documents, certificates, seals. This matches forging official documents.

Also possibly fraud (诈骗) because they obtained subsidy by deception. But the primary is forging documents to obtain subsidy. The list includes "诈骗" (fraud). In many cases, they label as 诈骗 when using false documents to obtain money. However examples: Insurance fraud case used "保险诈骗". For general fraud, they used "诈骗". Example: The case with "张某某" (multiple crimes) they used "盗窃;侵占". For forging documents they used "伪造、变造、买卖国家机关公文、证件、印章". So we should choose that.

Is there also "受贿"? No, he is not receiving bribe, he is forging documents for others. Not "贪污". Not "挪用公款". So answer: 伪造、变造、买卖国家机关公文、证件、印章.

Check if also "诈骗" needed. The act of forging documents to obtain subsidy is fraud. But the list includes "诈骗". In many examples, they used "诈骗" for cases where they deceived to get money, e.g., the case with "张某某" (multiple crimes) they used "盗窃;侵占". Not relevant. The case with "张某某" (the one with multiple crimes) they used "盗窃;侵占". The case with "张某某" (the one with forging documents) they used "伪造、变造、买卖国家机关公文、证件、印章". So we follow that.

Thus final answer: [罪名]伪造、变造、买卖国家机关公文、证件、印章<eoa>
